title: A Zendesk API token value with no email-and-token credential string around it
summary: A synthetic value alone in prose and a synthetic value in a JSON member named token, with no email address and no /token separator.
rationale: Zendesk documents the token only inside the {email_address}/token:{api_token} credential string and states no prefix, alphabet or length; its example is 40 characters of letters and digits, is labelled an example and is not said to be representative, and the only support for a 40-character run is consistency between two scanner rule artifacts. A bare value has no carrier and no grammar, so what is open is whether it belongs to this family. The three retirement phases (2026-07-28, 2026-10-27, 2027-04-30) are provider dates; it is not stated whether the first phase was applied or when the deprecation was announced, and those facts do not change what the carrier Cases assert.

expectation.rationale: No outcome is asserted for this family: the token grammar is not documented (open questions opaque-grammar and variants-over-time) and a bare value has no documented carrier. A Zendesk statement of the token format, or a documented carrier for a token alone, would settle it.

sources.supports: The example credential's token part is 40 characters of letters and digits; the page labels it Example and does not say it is representative of issued tokens.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. No outcome is asserted: the open question named in the expectation is what would have to be settled first.
